answer:
Here are the points I would raise at your check-up, most urgent first. These are things to ask about, not diagnoses; your doctor decides what to do.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide. The hospital stopped this water pill on March 5, 2026, because your sodium had fallen to 123. Some later lists still show it as active, and an eye clinic note from May 14, 2026 records you taking it. Please check whether you are still taking it. Your sodium was 134 in June, which is still a little low.

2. Thyroid recheck, overdue. Your TSH was high (7.9) in March. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6 to 8 weeks later. I found no repeat test in your records.

3. Lung nodule follow-up, overdue. A CT on October 18, 2025 found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lobe. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so that window closed on October 18, 2026. I found no chest CT in your records. Being a never smoker lowers the risk, but the follow-up still needs a decision.

4. Cholesterol and statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, HDL was 48 and triglycerides were 155. You have type 2 diabetes, and I see no statin on your medication list. I found no lipid test since September 2025.

5. Diabetes kidney test. I found no urine albumin test (UACR) in your records since your diabetes diagnosis. Your kidney filtration rate was normal in June (eGFR 71).

6. Diabetes is in good shape. Your A1c has fallen from 6.9 to 6.6, and your May 2026 dilated eye exam found no diabetic eye damage. The next eye exam is due around May 2027.

7. Kidney stone follow-up. The October 2025 discharge asked for a primary care follow-up in one week, and urology if the stone had not passed in two weeks. I found no urology visit and no repeat urine test, and the stone is still listed as active. Ask whether it has passed.

8. Vaccines and screening. The last flu shot in your records was on November 8, 2025, and this season's shot is not listed. Your records also have no mammogram and no cervical screening. These may have been done somewhere else.

9. Medication list clean-up. Several medicines appear more than once from different sources, such as Claritin (six entries), amlodipine, losartan and metformin. Bring your bottles or pharmacy printout to the visit so the list can be corrected.
